note: Every requirement from this Unit's nfr-requirements stage mapped to the design artifact and section that realises it. Where a design decision was reached by working a case against real PostgreSQL rather than by reasoning, the rationale says so and gives the result -- and where an earlier draft was WRONG, it says that too, because the corrected reasoning is the part a later reader needs. Three such corrections are recorded: the query-count bound, the migration test's vacuity, and the fold U3's guardian rows need before `role` can be dropped.

coverage.target: performance-design §B - INHERITED from U3 and first genuinely exercised here. U3's one-query lens resolution ran on routes that needed no lens; every U4 teacher route resolves one, so the single-statement shape now carries real traffic. The rename moves its index from account_id to student_account_id, which performance-design §B lists.

performance-design §A - INHERITED from U3: assert a query COUNT, never a duration. U4 extends the principle to list endpoints, where the property is CONSTANT IN N rather than a fixed number -- a literal count would reject selectinload.
performance-design §C - fetched_at is RENDERED, not merely stored. A stale read is V1's only offline state and hiding it is a lie of omission.
logical-components §C, performance-design §C - Room entities mirror the DTO plus fetched_at; a derived field is a business rule on the client.
performance-design §A - the count is CONSTANT IN N, not minimal. An `== 1` assertion would reject selectinload, which is correct and often preferable.
performance-design §A - two fixture sizes compared, both above one AND both below the batching chunk boundary. The second constraint was inverted in a draft and is now stated as a rule.
performance-design §A, §B - the guardian child list has the same constant-count property and a new index; U3 had no guardian column to index.
performance-design §B - four indexes for four reads. U3 created one because it had one query.
reliability-design §A - forward-only, no failover to fall back on.

reliability-design §A - RENAME, never drop-and-add. AND the FOLD: U3's guardian rows must merge into the student row before `role` is dropped, or every guardian appears on the roster as a pupil. That is a reshape, which 'renames preserve data' did not cover.
reliability-design §A - the lens rewrite ships in the same revision; separating them breaks authentication for everyone in the window.
reliability-design §A.1 - seeded rows AND a value assertion. Verified: empty table makes the shapes indistinguishable, and a row COUNT passes against both. Only the link survives or does not.
observability-design §A - display_name and guardian_phone are the first child-identifying strings in the system.
observability-design §A - enrollment_id only; it is already the teacher-facing key so this costs nothing.
observability-design §A - a reason CLASS, never the history found.
observability-design §B - nothing alerts, stated as a decision with its three reasons rather than as an omission.
observability-design §C - U4 writes no AuthAuditLog row; the closed enum is what keeps that log about authentication.
observability-design §C.1 - recorded as a COST decision, not a principled one, with a concrete revisit trigger: the first time U7 sends to guardian_phone.
scalability-design §B - phone lookup under U3's existing unique index.
reliability-design §B - batch plus subjects plus slots in one transaction.
scalability-design §B - Owner created lazily; most accounts never own a batch.
scalability-design §A - a unique index, verified against real PostgreSQL across seven cases.
scalability-design §A - PARTIAL on student_account_id IS NOT NULL. Without it the second dormant seat in a batch is refused, which is the normal early state.
reliability-design §B.
reliability-design §B - one row, asserted by count.
reliability-design §B - asserted at STATEMENT level, because there are no fee tables yet and a row-level assertion would pass vacuously.
security-design §A - owner_id comes from the lens object; there is no parameter to forge and no default to forget.
security-design §A - 404 on another owner's batch.
security-design §A - the two-teacher test, which B3 could not write because it had one party.
security-design §A - reachability through guardian_account_id, never through the child.
security-design §C - a test asserts no U4 module references Profile. The likely violation is a READ fallback, not a write.
security-design §C, Governance manifest - display_name and guardian_phone survive deletion; the teacher wrote them.
security-design §A, logical-components - Owner.state/plan/plan_valid_to only.
security-design §B, logical-components §A.2 - resolution fails CLOSED; failing open reattaches an erased student silently.
security-design §B - per-link markers, with the four states worked. Diverges from the catalogue and says so.
security-design §B.1 - two conditions. After erasure the first is true again, so a null-only test deletes the erased row and destroys the marker.
